spec: Task 005 stage 3b: extend(mesocycle, plan, logs, today, to), shorten(plan, logs, to), relength(plan, logs, cycle_number, days) and switch_rule(mesocycle, plan, logs, today, exercise_id, occurrence, from_cycle, rule). Each case names its op and args; expected is the edited plan (with dropped cycle numbers for shorten, and outcomes for switch_rule), or a refusal with its reason, cycle and day.

cases.name: extending the owner's 12-cycle block to 18 appends six cycles and changes nothing before them
cases.note: Task 005's criterion, FR-3.1c. Cycles 1-12 come back as they went in. Cycle 13 is one step past cycle 11 (65), and on to 75 at cycle 17; cycle 18 is a deload by the every-6 policy, 75 x 0.6 = 45.

cases.name: an extension carries a strategy switched mid-block
cases.note: Stage 3b decision 1: the new cycles take each exercise's latest rule. Cycles 2-3 were switched to double progression (7 then 8 at 40), so cycles 4-5 continue it: a load step and back to 6, then 7 — not linear.

cases.name: extending a plan stamped by a newer engine is refused
cases.note: Stage 3b decision 6: an extension projects, and this engine may not project over a newer one (INV-06).

cases.name: a block never grows past 52 cycles
shortening drops trailing projected cycles and changes nothing it keeps
cases.note: FR-3.1c: cycles 5 and 6 are dropped, for the wrapper to archive (INV-11).

cases.name: shortening refuses to drop a completed cycle
cases.note: Task 005's criterion, INV-06: cycle 3 is completed, so the block cannot end at 2.

cases.name: shortening refuses to drop a locked cycle until the user unlocks it
cases.note: Stage 3b decision 2: a pin means the engine keeps its hands off, dropping included.

cases.name: a block never shrinks below 2 cycles
one 5-day cycle among 7-day ones shifts every later start, a locked cycle with them
cases.note: Task 005's criterion, FR-3.1a, 03 §5. Cycle 3 becomes 5 days: cycle 4 starts on 10-24 rather than 10-26, cycle 5 on 10-31. Cycle 4 is locked and moves anyway — the move is the user's own — and every cycle changed is written as the user's. No load changes.

cases.name: the cycle in progress may be shortened — the travel case
cases.note: Stage 3b decision 3: cycle 2 is under way and becomes 5 days; cycles 3-5 follow it.

cases.name: a completed cycle's length is history
a length change refuses to move a completed cycle
cases.note: Task 005's criterion, INV-06: cycle 3 is completed, so cycle 2's length cannot change under it.

cases.name: a length change refuses to leave a session past the cycle's new end
cases.note: 03 §5, stage 3b decision 3: cycle 3 holds a session on day 7, so it cannot become 5 days until the user moves that session.

cases.name: switching linear_load to double_progression in cycle 5 continues from the load achieved
cases.note: Task 005's criterion, FR-3.6a. Cycle 4 planned 47.5 and was lifted at 50. From cycle 5 the squat is double progression 6-8: 7 at 50, 8 at 50, then a load step, 6 at 52.5 — from the 50 actually lifted, not from cycle 1's 40, and not from the plan's 47.5. Cycles 1-4 keep their linear rule.

cases.name: a switch leaves a locked cycle's rule alone, and continues from it
cases.note: Stage 3b decision 4: cycle 6 is locked at 55 under the linear rule and keeps both. Cycle 5 switches (7 at 50); cycle 7 steps from the locked cycle 6 as double progression: 7 at 55.

cases.name: switching on a plan stamped by a newer engine is refused
switching an exercise the plan does not hold is refused
